newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania slams opposition to Ukraine treaty.
newsitem.headline: Romania slams opposition to Ukraine treaty.

text.p: Romania vowed on Thursday to pursue efforts to sign a key treaty with neighbouring Ukraine which would boost Bucharest's chances of admission to NATO.
The foreign ministry used unusually strong words in a statement slamming propaganda opposing the pact -- which would settle World War Two issues -- as "unpatriotic".

It warned that "recent agitation" over Bucharest's drive to conclude the treaty with Kiev was "fuelled by circles alien to Romania's interests, which wanted the country to stay outside European and Euro-Atlantic structures."

Local media reported that hundreds of leaflets had been pasted overnight on buildings in the western city of Timisoara, calling for protests against the new centrist government's plans to speed up the treaty with ex-Soviet Ukraine.
Police in Timisoara, on the border with Hungary and Serbia, said they had launched an investigation to trace the anonymous authors of the leaflets.

The unsigned tracts said the treaty with Ukraine would mean Romania would "lose for ever the lands of Bucovina, Herta, southern Bessarabia and Serpent Island" -- a reference to former Romanian territory annexed by Moscow under a 1939 Nazi-Soviet pact and now part of Ukraine.
The latest round of talks ended in Kiev last week without a final agreement, but both sides acknowledged progress.
One remaining stumbling bloc focused on delineating frontiers in the Black Sea, where both sides are drilling for gas and oil.
Talks stalled last year over the former ruling leftists' insistence on some form of public atonement by Ukraine for the World War Two seizure by the Kremlin of Romanian lands.

But the centrists, who ousted ex-communists in elections last November, are keen to promote a new partnership with Ukraine and Poland, as part of their drive to bridge the gap separating their country from more developed East Europeans.
Bucharest hopes to sign the treaty with Ukraine -- after a similar one agreed last year with Hungary ending old rifts between neighbours over borders and ethnic minorities -- in "the near future".
Romania is lobbying for inclusion in NATO's first eastward expansion, to be announced at a July summit in Madrid.
